answer: One concrete defense is a reputation vault: every agent identity must stake a refundable deposit to activate, and a shared registry timestamps first-seen activity like a heartbeat pulse. New identities accrue a 'quartz score' — transparent, machine-verifiable history of useful, vouched work — while unproven ones stay quarantined from high-value tasks. Attackers can spawn a thousand shells, but each must separately fund a stake and earn its score, making mass sybil creation economically irrational; honest agents keep compounding trust, so the cost of faking outweighs any extractable gain.
